meta.description: A policy problem-instrument map derived from Ohno's Learning to Industrialize. Seven concrete root problems replace the single abstract 'middle-income trap' root. Each root is directly mappable to policy instruments.

problems.name: Low Enterprise Productivity and Quality
problems.statement: Domestic firms, especially SMEs, operate with low productivity and poor quality, limiting their ability to compete and upgrade.
problems.description: Weak firm-level capability is a root cause of failed industrial upgrading. SMEs lack management, technical, and quality control capabilities, and cannot absorb technology effectively.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Missing Supporting Industries and Weak FDI Linkages
problems.statement: Domestic supporting industries are too weak to supply core firms, and FDI operates in enclaves with few local linkages.
problems.description: Without supplier development and local absorptive capacity, FDI generates limited spillovers. Supporting industries are essential for clustering and value chain integration.
goals: Integrate local firms into value chains

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Shortage of Industrial Human Resources
problems.statement: There is a critical shortage of engineers, technicians, managers, and skilled workers needed for industrial upgrading.
problems.description: Industrialization requires a critical mass of capable people who can absorb, adapt, and create technology. TVET systems are disconnected from industry needs, and skill mismatch is widespread.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Financial Constraints for Industrial Investment
problems.statement: Firms, especially SMEs, cannot obtain adequate finance for equipment, technology, and working capital.
problems.description: Financial constraints prevent firms from upgrading. Collateral requirements, weak credit information, and lack of long-term finance are key obstacles.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Policy Process and Governance
problems.statement: Government lacks the capability to design, implement, and adapt industrial policies suited to local conditions.
problems.description: Policy capacity includes diagnosis, dialogue with the private sector, learning from international experience, coordination across agencies, and implementation discipline.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 6-7). Routledge.

problems.name: Infrastructure and Business Environment Bottlenecks
problems.statement: Poor infrastructure, logistics, and administrative burden raise costs and reduce industrial competitiveness.
problems.description: Reliable power, transport, industrial parks, and efficient administration are necessary for industrial investment and cluster development.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Dependence on Given Growth Sources
problems.statement: Growth depends on externally given advantages—resources, aid, big projects, or FDI enclaves—rather than on created value.
problems.description: Given growth arises from FDI, aid, resource rents, or large public projects. It can produce temporary growth but does not build endogenous industrial capability.
goals: Reduce dependence on exogenous growth sources
Convert given advantages into created advantages
Balance big projects with broad industrial support

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 1-2). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak SME Management and Technology Capability
problems.statement: SMEs lack management, technical, and quality control capabilities.
problems.description: SME upgrading is central to industrial deepening. Without it, domestic firms cannot supply MNCs or compete in export markets.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Poor Quality and Productivity
problems.statement: Firms produce low-quality goods with high defect rates and low productivity.
problems.description: Quality and productivity problems limit market access and upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Low Technology Absorption
problems.statement: Firms cannot absorb, adapt, and improve imported technology.
problems.description: Technology absorption requires technical skills, enterprise effort, and supporting institutions.
goals: Adapt foreign technology to local conditions

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 4-5). Routledge.

problems.name: Missing Supporting Industries
problems.statement: Domestic supporting industries are too weak to supply core firms.
problems.description: Supporting industries are essential for clustering and FDI linkage. Their absence raises import dependence and limits spillovers.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Local Suppliers Cannot Meet MNC Standards
problems.statement: Local firms cannot meet the quality, cost, and delivery standards of multinational buyers.
problems.description: This blocks FDI-local linkage and limits spillovers.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Linkage Programs
problems.statement: There are few effective programs to connect FDI with local firms.
problems.description: Linkage requires systematic matching, supplier development, and monitoring.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Low Local Absorptive Capacity
problems.statement: Local firms and workers cannot absorb knowledge transferred from FDI.
problems.description: Absorptive capacity depends on skills, management, and technology capability.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 3 and 5). Routledge.

problems.name: FDI Enclave Economy
problems.statement: FDI operates in enclaves with few links to the domestic economy.
problems.description: Without supplier development and local absorptive capacity, FDI generates limited spillovers.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Shortage of Engineers and Technicians
problems.statement: There are too few engineers and technicians for industrial upgrading.
problems.description: Engineering and technical skills are prerequisites for technology absorption and high-value production.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak TVET System
problems.statement: Technical and vocational education is disconnected from industry needs.
problems.description: TVET systems often lack equipment, qualified instructors, and industry participation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Shortage of Industrial Managers
problems.statement: Firms lack managers with industrial and quality management skills.
problems.description: Management capability is critical for productivity, quality, and technology adoption.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Skill Mismatch
problems.statement: Workers' skills do not match the needs of growing industries.
problems.description: Skill mismatch reduces productivity and increases unemployment among graduates.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Collateral Constraints
problems.statement: SMEs cannot provide sufficient collateral for bank loans.
problems.description: Collateral requirements exclude many viable SMEs from credit.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Credit Information
problems.statement: Banks lack reliable information to assess SME creditworthiness.
problems.description: Information asymmetry raises lending costs and reduces credit access.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Lack of Long-Term Industrial Finance
problems.statement: Firms cannot obtain long-term finance for capital investment.
problems.description: Long-term finance is needed for equipment, technology, and industrial upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: SME Finance Gap
problems.statement: SMEs face a persistent gap in access to affordable credit.
problems.description: SME finance gaps constrain upgrading and job creation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Random Policy Copying
problems.statement: Policies are copied from abroad without adaptation to local conditions.
problems.description: Policy copying without local diagnosis and ownership leads to poor implementation and weak results.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 6-7). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Coordination Across Agencies
problems.statement: Ministries and agencies pursue inconsistent industrial policies.
problems.description: Coordination failure causes duplication, inconsistent incentives, and weak implementation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Implementation Capacity
problems.statement: Policies are announced but not implemented effectively.
problems.description: Implementation requires administrative capacity, monitoring, and feedback.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 7). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Public-Private Dialogue
problems.statement: Government and private sector do not communicate effectively on industrial policy.
problems.description: Without dialogue, policies may not address real constraints and firms may not support implementation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Unreliable Power Supply
problems.statement: Firms face power outages and high energy costs.
problems.description: Unreliable power disrupts production and raises costs.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: High Logistics Costs
problems.statement: Poor transport and logistics raise export and input costs.
problems.description: High logistics costs reduce competitiveness and discourage investment.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Poor Industrial Parks
problems.statement: Industrial parks lack infrastructure, services, and effective management.
problems.description: Well-managed parks reduce investment costs and facilitate clustering.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Administrative Burden
problems.statement: Complex regulations and procedures raise costs and delay investment.
problems.description: Administrative burden discourages formal investment and firm growth.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Resource Dependence
problems.statement: The economy relies on natural resource rents rather than productive value creation.
problems.description: Resource dependence can weaken incentives for industrial learning and diversify poorly into manufacturing.
goals: Use resource revenues for industrial capability

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 1). Routledge.

problems.name: Aid Dependence
problems.statement: Development aid substitutes for domestic policy effort and private investment.
problems.description: Aid can help but may also create dependency if it does not build local capability and policy ownership.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Big Project Bias
problems.statement: Policy favors large showcase projects over broad-based firm and skill development.
problems.description: Big projects can be politically attractive but may not generate widespread industrial learning or SME upgrading.
goals: Balance big projects with broad industrial support
Link large projects to local suppliers

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 1 and 6). Routledge.

instruments.name: Continuous Improvement
instruments.description: Continuous improvement of productivity and quality through small, incremental changes involving all workers.
instruments.mechanism: Hands-on training and practice on the factory floor, often supported by national movements and foreign experts.

caseStudies.label: Ethiopia Kaizen Movement
caseStudies.note: JICA-supported Kaizen unit in Ethiopia led to productivity improvements in pilot firms and was scaled into a national movement.

caseStudies.label: Japan Toyota Production System
caseStudies.note: Kaizen is a core element of Japanese industrial competitiveness.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Shindan / Enterprise Diagnosis
instruments.description: A systematic enterprise evaluation and advice system where consultants diagnose management and technical problems and recommend improvements.
instruments.mechanism: Institutionalized diagnostic service provided by government or accredited consultants, often linked to SME finance.

caseStudies.label: Japan Shindan System
caseStudies.note: Japan's SME diagnosis system has been a model for many East Asian economies for enterprise upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Credit Guarantee System
instruments.description: A scheme where the government or a public entity guarantees a portion of loans made by commercial banks to SMEs, reducing lender risk.
instruments.mechanism: Risk-sharing between government and banks, often combined with enterprise evaluation.

caseStudies.label: Taiwan SME Credit Guarantee Fund
caseStudies.note: Taiwan's credit guarantee fund has been instrumental in supporting SME development.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Two-Step Loans
instruments.description: Government funds are channeled through commercial banks to targeted firms at subsidized rates, with banks responsible for appraisal and monitoring.
instruments.mechanism: Wholesale funds from a development financial institution to retail banks for on-lending to priority sectors.

caseStudies.label: Japan Two-Step Loan
caseStudies.note: Used extensively in post-war Japan to direct credit to strategic industries.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Investment Incentives
instruments.description: Fiscal and non-fiscal incentives such as tax holidays, duty exemptions, and subsidies targeted at priority activities.
instruments.mechanism: A list of priority activities linked to a system of incentives, often administered by investment promotion agencies.

caseStudies.label: Singapore Economic Development Board
caseStudies.note: Singapore's EDB used targeted incentives to attract high-value FDI.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Industrial Parks
instruments.description: Dedicated estates with sufficient infrastructure and administrative services to facilitate industrial clustering and FDI.
instruments.mechanism: Provision of serviced land and facilities, often including one-stop administrative services.

caseStudies.label: Taiwan Export Processing Zones
caseStudies.note: Taiwan's EPZs were pioneers in providing integrated infrastructure and services for export-oriented industrialization.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Technical and Vocational Education and Training
instruments.description: Formal and non-formal training programs to build technical skills for new or current workers, often linked to industry needs.
instruments.mechanism: Curricula development, training delivery, skill certification, and industry partnerships.

caseStudies.label: Singapore Vocational Training
caseStudies.note: Singapore's ITE and polytechnic system is a key pillar of its industrial human resource strategy.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

instruments.name: Policy Dialogue
instruments.description: Structured, continuous dialogue between government, private sector, and foreign experts to diagnose problems and formulate concrete policies.
instruments.mechanism: Regular meetings, joint working groups, study tours, and coaching by experts.

caseStudies.label: Ethiopia-Japan Policy Dialogue
caseStudies.note: The dialogue led to concrete proposals on Kaizen, public-private cooperation, and action plan making.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

instruments.name: Human Resource Development Fund
instruments.description: A dedicated fund to finance training, technology transfer, and skill certification.
instruments.mechanism: Pooled resources from levies on firms or government budget used to subsidize training costs.

caseStudies.label: Malaysia Human Resource Development Fund
caseStudies.note: Malaysia's HRDF mandates contributions from employers to fund training.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

instruments.name: Anchor Firm Attraction
instruments.description: Targeted attraction of a large, globally competitive firm to catalyze local supplier development.
instruments.mechanism: Customized incentives and infrastructure provision for a single large investor, followed by supplier development.

caseStudies.label: Malaysia Penang Cluster
caseStudies.note: Attracting Intel and other MNCs catalyzed Penang's electronics cluster.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Supplier Development Program
instruments.description: Programs to upgrade local suppliers to meet the quality, cost, and delivery standards of large buyers.
instruments.mechanism: Diagnosis, training, technical assistance, and matching with MNCs.

caseStudies.label: Malaysia Vendor Development
caseStudies.note: Malaysia used vendor development to link local firms with MNCs.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Export Processing Zones
instruments.description: Special zones with infrastructure and incentives for export-oriented manufacturing.
instruments.mechanism: Duty-free inputs, serviced land, and streamlined administration.

caseStudies.label: Taiwan Export Processing Zones
caseStudies.note: Taiwan's EPZs helped launch export-led industrialization.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Policy Learning Unit
instruments.description: A dedicated government unit for comparative policy analysis, diagnosis, and policy adaptation.
instruments.mechanism: Research, study tours, expert networks, and policy experimentation.

caseStudies.label: Ethiopia Policy Learning
caseStudies.note: Policy learning helped Ethiopia formulate concrete industrial policy actions.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 7). Routledge.

instruments.name: Technical Extension Services
instruments.description: Public or publicly supported services that provide firms with technical advice and problem-solving support.
instruments.mechanism: Visits by engineers and consultants, demonstrations, and joint problem-solving.

caseStudies.label: Japan Kogyo Shikenjo
caseStudies.note: Japan's industrial research institutes provided technical extension to SMEs.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: SME Credit Information System
instruments.description: A system to collect and share credit information on SMEs, reducing information asymmetry.
instruments.mechanism: Databases, credit scoring, and sharing among banks.

caseStudies.label: Japan Credit Information
caseStudies.note: Japan developed credit information systems to support SME lending.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: One-Stop Investment and Administrative Service
instruments.description: A single agency or office that handles permits, licenses, and administrative procedures for investors.
instruments.mechanism: Co-location of officials, simplified procedures, and time-bound approvals.

caseStudies.label: Singapore EDB One-Stop Service
caseStudies.note: Singapore's EDB provided integrated investor services.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Industrial Infrastructure Provision
instruments.description: Public investment in power, water, transport, and other infrastructure needed by industry.
instruments.mechanism: Direct public investment or public-private partnerships.

caseStudies.label: East Asian Infrastructure
caseStudies.note: East Asian economies invested heavily in industrial infrastructure.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Industrial Cluster Development
instruments.description: Policies to promote geographic concentration and interaction among firms, suppliers, and institutions.
instruments.mechanism: Infrastructure, shared services, supplier networks, and cluster governance.

caseStudies.label: Penang Electronics Cluster
caseStudies.note: Penang developed a successful electronics cluster through FDI and supplier development.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Trade Logistics Improvement
instruments.description: Measures to reduce logistics costs and improve transport and trade facilitation.
instruments.mechanism: Ports, roads, customs reform, and logistics services.

caseStudies.label: Singapore Logistics
caseStudies.note: Singapore's world-class logistics supported its industrial and trade competitiveness.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Industrial Master Plan
instruments.description: A strategic document that sets industrial priorities, targets, and policy measures.
instruments.mechanism: Diagnosis, vision, prioritized sectors, action plans, and monitoring.

caseStudies.label: Malaysia Industrial Master Plan
caseStudies.note: Malaysia used industrial master plans to guide structural change.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

instruments.name: Business Law and Regulatory Reform
instruments.description: Reform of laws and regulations to reduce administrative burden and improve the business environment.
instruments.mechanism: Simplification, transparency, and legal modernization.

caseStudies.label: Vietnam Business Law Reform
caseStudies.note: Vietnam reformed business laws to encourage private enterprise.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Quality Control Circles
instruments.description: Small groups of workers who meet regularly to solve quality and productivity problems.
instruments.mechanism: Worker participation, problem-solving, and continuous improvement.

caseStudies.label: Japan QC Circles
caseStudies.note: QC circles became widespread in Japanese manufacturing.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Public-Private Policy Council
instruments.description: A formal council for dialogue and coordination between government and private sector.
instruments.mechanism: Regular meetings, working groups, and joint policy recommendations.

caseStudies.label: Japan Industrial Policy Councils
caseStudies.note: Japan used councils to coordinate industrial policy with the private sector.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

instruments.name: Skill Certification
instruments.description: A system to assess and certify workers' skills, improving labor market information and training incentives.
instruments.mechanism: Standards, testing, and certification bodies.

caseStudies.label: Singapore Skill Certification
caseStudies.note: Singapore developed skill certification to support its workforce upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

instruments.name: Development Financial Institution
instruments.description: A public or semi-public financial institution that provides long-term industrial finance.
instruments.mechanism: Direct lending, wholesale funds, and policy-based finance.

caseStudies.label: Japan Development Bank
caseStudies.note: Japan's Development Bank provided long-term finance for industrial upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Equipment Leasing
instruments.description: Leasing arrangements that allow firms to use equipment without large upfront collateral.
instruments.mechanism: Lease finance, tax incentives, and specialized leasing companies.

caseStudies.label: East Asian Leasing
caseStudies.note: Equipment leasing helped SMEs invest in machinery.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

instruments.name: Targeted FDI Marketing
instruments.description: Proactive targeting of specific foreign investors to fill gaps in the industrial structure.
instruments.mechanism: Investment promotion, customized incentives, and aftercare.

caseStudies.label: Singapore EDB Targeting
caseStudies.note: Singapore targeted high-value MNCs to build new industries.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Technology Transfer Program
instruments.description: Programs to facilitate the transfer of technology from foreign firms, research institutes, or experts to local firms.
instruments.mechanism: Technical cooperation, licensing support, and joint projects.

caseStudies.label: Japan Technology Transfer
caseStudies.note: Japan absorbed and adapted foreign technology during industrialization.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 4-5). Routledge.

instruments.name: Export Promotion
instruments.description: Measures to help firms enter export markets and meet international standards.
instruments.mechanism: Export financing, trade fairs, market information, and quality certification.

caseStudies.label: East Asian Export Promotion
caseStudies.note: Export promotion was central to East Asian industrialization.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

instruments.name: Local Supplier Database
instruments.description: A database of local suppliers that helps MNCs identify and source from domestic firms.
instruments.mechanism: Supplier registration, capability profiling, and matching services.

caseStudies.label: Malaysia Supplier Database
caseStudies.note: Malaysia used supplier databases to promote FDI-local linkage.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.
